_comment: VISUAL SURVEY — CURATION, not measurement. Judgements made by
HILLSHADING each stamp and LOOKING at it.
This exists because `tag_source: "filename"` is a GUESS. A tag matched
against a filename records what the vendor called the file, not what
the pixels contain. The pixels are ground truth; the filename is a
Surveyed 2026-08-03 for the alpine region composition. Evidence:
scripts/catalogue_heightmaps.py merges this in and sets
tag_source = "visual" for every entry named here, so the trust tier
survives regeneration of the catalogue. Entries NOT named here keep
tag_source = "filename" and must be looked at before being trusted.
`character` is what the stamp ACTUALLY depicts. `alpine` is whether it
belongs in an alpine composition, and is a judgement about THIS region,
not a quality score — a desert butte is not a bad stamp.

HM_Rugged_Rocks_14_Ex.png.character: circular radial dome with a crater-like centre
HM_Rugged_Rocks_14_Ex.png.note: Filename tag said `outcrop`. IT IS NOT AN OUTCROP. This was the ONE placement already committed to the recipe (`east_ridge_outcrops`, ADD 180 m) and it would have put a round bump on the east ridge. Caught only by looking.

HM_Rugged_Rocks_02_Ex.png.note: Filename tag `outcrop`; same radial family as _14.

HM_Terraced_Cliffs_06_Ex.png.note: Filename tag `cliffs`. It is a cone, not a cliff band.

HM_Terraced_Cliffs_Drake_Ex.png.note: Filename tag `cliffs`. Same cone family as _06.

HM_Monument_Desert_02_Ex.png.character: isolated desert buttes on a flat pan
HM_Monument_Desert_02_Ex.png.note: Correct for arid mesa country, wrong biome for alpine. Not a defect in the stamp.

HM_Terrace_Fields_15_Ex.png.character: man-made agricultural terracing, contour-following field walls
HM_Terrace_Fields_15_Ex.png.note: Filename tag `terrace` reads as a geological terrace. It is ANTHROPOGENIC. Would imply farming culture wherever placed — a world-building statement, not a landform.

HM_Dover_Cliffs_06_Ex.png.character: rounded chalk downland, soft convex hills
HM_Dover_Cliffs_06_Ex.png.note: A real cliff formation, but far too soft and rounded to read as alpine. Usable in a temperate coastal region.

HM_Dover_Cliffs_15_Ex.png.character: rounded chalk downland, soft convex hills

HM_Rough_Cliffs_18_Ex.png.character: sharp jagged high-relief arêtes with deep shadowed faces
HM_Rough_Cliffs_18_Ex.png.note: The best summit-massif stamp in the collection. Used as summit_massif_north.

HM_Seaside_Cliffs_02_Ex.png.character: parallel knife-edge spurs separated by deep linear troughs
HM_Seaside_Cliffs_02_Ex.png.note: Despite the name, reads as a parallel arête system. Used as spine_aretes.

HM_Seaside_Cliffs_06_Ex.png.character: parallel spur-and-trough system, slightly softer than _02

HM_Pride_Rocks_02_Ex.png.character: angular blocky rock mass with sharp planar faces

HM_Pride_Rocks_11_Ex.png.character: angular rock mass, more dissected than _02

HM_Pride_Rocks_01_Ex.png.note: One big mass, less articulated than _02/_11.

HM_Valleys_01_Ex.png.note: Used as drainage_south with MIN to carve.

HM_Terraced_Cliffs_01_Ex.png.character: linear stepped cliff band, genuine geological terracing
HM_Terraced_Cliffs_01_Ex.png.note: The only true cliff BAND. Used as cliff_band_west. Unlike _06/_Drake this one matches its filename.

HM_Rugged_Sedi_Rocks_24_Ex.png.character: scattered low rock knolls on a broad surface
HM_Rugged_Sedi_Rocks_24_Ex.png.note: Used as outcrops_mid for mid-slope outcrop scatter.

HM_Rugged_Sedi_Rocks_08_Ex.png.character: one large sedimentary mass with a steep face

HM_Rolling_Hills_06_Ex.png.note: Sharper than the name suggests. Foothill texture.

HM_Meadows_04_Ex.png.character: softly dissected low relief with broad open floors
HM_Meadows_04_Ex.png.note: Used as foothill_basin_southwest with MIN to cap elevation.

HM_Meadows_28_Ex.png.note: Used as foothill_basin_east with MIN to cap elevation.

HM_Meadows_12_Ex.png.note: Too flat to carry a basin floor on its own.

HM_Canyon_04_Ex.png.character: broad incised canyon with terraced walls
HM_Canyon_04_Ex.png.note: Reads arid; usable if the drainage is deep.

HM_Canyon_18_Ex.png.character: ridge mass cut by a deep canyon

HM_Canyon_Shapes_03_Ex.png.note: The right angles read as authored, not eroded.

HM_Rocky_Plateaus_01_Ex.png.character: single broad plateau mass with steep flanks
HM_Rocky_Plateaus_01_Ex.png.note: Usable as a shoulder or bench.

HM_Rugged_Rocks_20_Ex.png.note: Good low-amplitude detail overlay; not a landform on its own.
